sections.overview: This Beringian freshwater fish inhabits Alaska, nearby Bering Sea islands and northeastern Siberia.
sections.identification: Its broad, flattened head, large paddle-like pectoral fins and tiny pelvic fins distinguish it from other northern fishes.
sections.habitat: It occupies vegetated lowland ponds, lakes, sloughs and slow streams that may become oxygen-poor beneath winter ice.
sections.diet: It is an opportunistic feeder on small aquatic invertebrates, with fish also recorded in some populations and habitats.
sections.behavior: It can breathe air and tolerate very low dissolved oxygen, adaptations that help it persist in cold, ice-covered waters.
sections.reproduction: In Alaska, spawning occurs over an extended warm-season period, and females may release eggs in several batches.
sections.ecology: Its air-breathing physiology is unusual among Arctic fishes; local studies of transplanted populations also show that diet varies by waterbody.
sections.conservation: Alaska’s wildlife plan identifies it as a Species of Conservation Need, while USGS separately documents human-transplanted populations outside its native range.
